Multi-caller consensus iSNV detection

Source: R/consensus.R
consensusISNV.Rd

Takes a named list of WithinHostExperiment objects (one per variant caller) and identifies variant sites detected by multiple callers. Sites are matched by genomic position (seqnames + start) and alternative allele. Only sites detected by at least min_callers with a frequency spread no greater than freq_tolerance are retained.

Usage

consensusISNV(whe_list, min_callers = 2L, freq_tolerance = 0.05)

Arguments

whe_list

A named list of WithinHostExperiment objects, one per variant caller (e.g., list(ivar = whe1, lofreq = whe2)).

min_callers

Integer scalar. Minimum number of callers that must detect a site (default: 2L).

freq_tolerance

Numeric scalar. Maximum allowed range (max - min) of allele frequencies across callers for a site to pass (default: 0.05); a range equal to it, to within rounding error, passes.

Value

A WithinHostExperiment containing only consensus sites, with a column for every sample of the inputs. mcols(rowRanges) includes:

n_callers

Number of callers detecting the site; a caller that lists the same site and allele twice counts once.

caller_names

Comma-separated caller names.

freq_spread

Range of the allele frequencies of the calls, across callers.

Where a site passes in more than one sample, these three columns describe one of those samples, not all of them.

The altFreq assay contains the mean frequency of the calls for each consensus site and NA where the site did not pass in that sample, so a sample with no consensus site is a column of NA. Every call enters the mean and the spread, so a caller that lists a site twice is weighted twice there, though it counts once in n_callers. A sample held by fewer than min_callers inputs cannot reach consensus; it is kept as a column of NA, with a warning naming it, since that column would otherwise read as a sample without iSNVs. The constructor adds a qcPass assay that is TRUE throughout. Read counts, depths and the QC history are not carried over, so run flagISNV on the individual callers' objects rather than on the consensus.

The seqinfo() of the result merges those of the inputs; a sequence whose length, circularity or genome differs between inputs is an error. Each sample's colData row comes from the first input that holds the sample, so host, role and transmission-pair columns carry over.

Details

When technical replicates are unavailable, using a multi-caller consensus is recommended for reducing false positive iSNV calls (Roder et al. 2023).

References

Roder AE et al. (2023). Optimized quantification of intra-host viral diversity in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus sequence data. mBio 14:e01046-23. doi:10.1128/mbio.01046-23

Examples

gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200, 300), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "C", "G")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("T", "G", "A")
whe1 <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = matrix(c(0.10, 0.20, 0.30), ncol = 1)),
    rowRanges = gr, colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "S1"))
gr2 <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200, 400), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr2)$ref <- c("A", "C", "T")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr2)$alt <- c("T", "G", "C")
whe2 <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = matrix(c(0.12, 0.18, 0.15), ncol = 1)),
    rowRanges = gr2, colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "S1"))
consensus <- consensusISNV(list(caller1 = whe1, caller2 = whe2))
consensus
#> WithinHostExperiment with 2 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(2): altFreq, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 0 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0
